title: Lodestar prompt heuristics diary
content:
Quick diary / sketchpad for odd heuristics and tiny template sets I keep reaching for. Mostly messy — notes to self and reproducible examples to drop into eval harness later.

Context / motivation:
- Trying to compress a robust instruction template that survives model switching (Llama2-13B -> open-llm-translate -> quantized variants).
- Primary constraints: token budget <= 120, single-turn user prompt (no system message), prefer explicit canonicalization steps.
- Observed failure modes: hallucinated list items, refusal drift, repetition loops for enumerations, over-constraining leading to terse outputs.

Principles I keep coming back to (working):
1) Anchor + Example + Format: 1 short anchor sentence (role + goal), 1 minimal exemplar output, then format spec.
2) Guard clauses to prevent hallucination: ask model to "only use the facts provided below" when examples include invented facts.
3) Soft temperature hints: when switching to smaller models, prefer more explicit exemplar diversity rather than low temperature.
4) Token budgeting: use placeholder tokens for long contexts ("[CTX_SNIPPET]") and explicit truncation instructions.

Small templates & few-shot sets (copyable):
- TEMPLATE A (compact anchor + exemplar):
  Anchor: "You are a concise fact-check assistant."
  Example: "Q: Who invented X? A: Name (year)."
  Format: "Answer in one sentence. If unknown, say 'Unknown'."
  TO-USE: prepend 1–2 short context lines then the Qs.

- TEMPLATE B (enumeration safety):
  Anchor: "List only items that appear in the passage below; do not invent."
  Exemplar: "Passage: ...
  Q: List the causes mentioned.
  A: 1) cause A; 2) cause B."
  Failure note: with Llama2-13B-quantized, it still added a 3rd item ~30% cases. Tried anchor stronger: "If the passage lists N causes, list N; do not add any others, and if none, say 'none listed'." Reduced error but made it sometimes reply 'none listed' incorrectly (over-pruning).

- TEMPLATE C (roleplay + persona tilt):
  Anchor: "You are a meticulous editor. Focus on clarity and noun-verb alignment."
  Exemplar: "IN: messy sentence -> OUT: cleaned sentence"
  Notes: Good for instruction-following, but sensitive to few-shot wording (if exemplar too prescriptive, model parrots structure).

Mini few-shot bank (3-shot compact; each example <= 18 tokens):
1) Q: "Summarize in one line: [short article]" -> A: one-line summary.
2) Q: "Extract the core claim:" -> A: single clause.
3) Q: "Tone-check: is the language neutral? Answer yes/no + one reason."

Observed failure cases (examples recorded during runs):
- Case F1: enumeration hallucination (see TEMPLATE B). Model invents plausible-sounding items.
  Quick mitigation attempted: append 'If you are guessing, write "(guess)" after any uncertain item.' This reduces confidence but sometimes increases verbosity.

- Case F2: chaining collapse. With multi-step examples the model skips step 2 and returns final inference without intermediate checks. Happens more with quantized runtimes. Mitigation: explicitly enumerate steps required and mark each with a label (STEP 1:, STEP 2:).

- Case F3: out-of-scope politely refuses even when data present. Some models prefer safety bias after few-shot that hints at refusal. Fix: add a line 'If the necessary information is present in the passage, answer without refusal.'

Quick experiments (short results):
- Run 1 (Llama2-13B, default quant): Template A, 100 prompts -> exact instruction adherence 62%
- Run 2 (gpt-3.5-like opt, fp16): Template A, 100 prompts -> adherence 74% but more verbose answers
- Run 3 (llama2-13B-8bit): TEMPLATE B enumeration tests 200 prompts -> hallucination rate 28%
Notes: need stable eval harness, these were manual runs via local runner.

Ideas / TODOs:
- Convert the 3-shot bank into JSONL for regression tests. (TODO: write script to auto-create token-limited shots)
- Try soft-instruction augmentation: add a trailing instruction 'Prefer short, factual responses (<= 28 tokens).' Measure tradeoff of factuality vs. recall.
- Add a 'uncertainty token' strategy: ask model to include a confidence label (high/med/low) after each item. Evaluate calibration.
- Check effect of placement: system-like anchor at the top vs. inline just before Q. Hypothesis: small models prefer inline anchor (put this in bench matrix).

Notes to self about eval design:
- Keep diversity in few-shot exemplars (avoid identical phrasing).
- Track per-token latency + adherence; some heuristics increase tokens enough to blow budget.
- For private deployments, test with quantized variants from the same model family to ensure stability.

Random snippets / mental notes:
- "Anchor in 6 words or less" seems to perform better than long role paragraphs.
- When the exemplar contains an explicit marker like "[EX]", the model sometimes copies the marker; test stripping markers in postproc.
- Avoid 'You are allowed to use common sense' phrasing — yields creative but sometimes incorrect inference.

Logs & references I should attach to eval PR:
- sample_output_f1.csv (local) -> shows 50 examples of enumeration hallucination
- bench-config.yaml -> includes temperature, tokens, truncation rules used

End of current patch of notes. Will re-run small bench on 2026-03-05 with updated anchor phrasing and record results here.

-- Marissa
